Hello!
I have recently encountered a puzzling behaviour regarding lean's typeclass inference.
Essentially, I have to infer some instance for an application where the left term is a function.
The issue is that the inference fails unless I define an abbreviation for this function.

The code is the following :

import Iris
import Std.Data.TreeMap
open Std Iris
-- OFE is some random class from Iris
-- the following instance is defined somewhere
-- instance instOFE [PartialMap M K] [OFE V] : OFE (M V)
instance : OFE ((TreeMap Nat · compare) Unit) := by infer_instance
-- the line above fails even though we do have the needed instances to use
-- instOFE as the following succed
instance : Std.PartialMap (TreeMap Nat · compare) Nat := by infer_instance
instance : OFE Unit := by infer_instance
-- adding an abbreviation solves the issue
abbrev FinMap := (TreeMap Nat · compare)
instance : OFE (FinMap Unit) := by infer_instance
-- the line above succeed as expected

I also have the debug traces obtained with

set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true
set_option trace.Meta.isDefEq true
set_option trace.Meta.isDefEq.assign true

trace for the unsuccessful typeclass resolution

[Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) =?= ?m.5 ▶
[Meta.synthInstance] ❌️ OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▼
  [] ✅️ new goal OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▶
  [apply] ❌️ apply @PartialMap.instOFE to OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▼
    [tryResolve] ❌️ OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ≟ OFE (?m.8 ?m.10) ▼
      [isDefEq] ❌️ OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) =?= OFE (?m.8 ?m.10) ▼
        [] ❌️ (fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit =?= ?m.8 ?m.10 ▼
          [] (fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit [nonassignable] =?= ?m.8 ?m.10 [assignable]
          [assign] ❌️ ?m.8 ?m.10 := (fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit ▼
            [foApprox] ?m.8 [?m.10] := (fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit
            [] ❌️ ?m.10 =?= compare ▼
              [] ?m.10 [assignable] =?= compare [nonassignable]
              [assign] ❌️ ?m.10 := compare ▼
                [beforeMkLambda] ?m.10 [] := compare
                [checkTypes] ❌️ (?m.10 : Type ?u.54) := (compare : Nat → Nat → Ordering) ▼
                  [] ❌️ Type ?u.54 =?= Nat → Nat → Ordering ▼
                    [onFailure] ❌️ Type ?u.54 =?= Nat → Nat → Ordering
              [assign] ❌️ ?m.10 := fun x y => compareOfLessAndEq x y ▼
                [beforeMkLambda] ?m.10 [] := fun x y => compareOfLessAndEq x y
                [checkTypes] ❌️ (?m.10 : Type ?u.54) := (fun x y => compareOfLessAndEq x y : Nat → Nat → Ordering) ▼
                  [] ❌️ Type ?u.54 =?= Nat → Nat → Ordering
            [constApprox] ?m.8 [?m.10] := (fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit
          [assign] ❌️ ?m.8 ?m.10 := TreeMap Nat Unit compare ▼
            [foApprox] ?m.8 [?m.10] := TreeMap Nat Unit compare
            [] ❌️ ?m.10 =?= compare ▼
              [] ?m.10 [assignable] =?= compare [nonassignable]
              [assign] ❌️ ?m.10 := compare ▼
                [beforeMkLambda] ?m.10 [] := compare
                [checkTypes] ❌️ (?m.10 : Type ?u.54) := (compare : Nat → Nat → Ordering) ▼

                    [onFailure] ❌️ Type ?u.54 =?= Nat → Nat → Ordering

                [beforeMkLambda] ?m.10 [] := fun x y => compareOfLessAndEq x y
                [checkTypes] ❌️ (?m.10 : Type ?u.54) := (fun x y => compareOfLessAndEq x y : Nat → Nat → Ordering) ▼

        [onFailure] ❌️ OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) =?= OFE (?m.8 ?m.10)
        [onFailure] ❌️ OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) =?= OFE (?m.8 ?m.10)
  [apply] ✅️ apply @CMRA.toOFE to OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▶
  [apply] ❌️ apply @Heap.instStoreCMRA to CMRA ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▶
  [apply] ❌️ apply @RFunctor.cmra to CMRA ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▶
  [apply] ✅️ apply @UCMRA.toCMRA to CMRA ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▶

  [] result <not-available>
[Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) =?= OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit)

trace for the successfull typeclass inference (with the abbrev)

-- [Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ OFE (FinMap Unit) =?= ?m.2 ▶
-- [Meta.synthInstance] ✅️ OFE (FinMap Unit) ▼
--   [] ✅️ new goal OFE (FinMap Unit) ▼
--     [instances] #[@COFE.toOFE, @COFE.OFunctor.cofe, @CMRA.toOFE, @PartialMap.instOFE, instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2]
--   [apply] ✅️ apply instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2 to OFE (FinMap Unit) ▼
--     [tryResolve] ✅️ OFE (FinMap Unit) ≟ OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▼
--       [isDefEq] ✅️ OFE (FinMap Unit) =?= OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▼
--         [] ✅️ FinMap Unit =?= (fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit ▼
--           [] ✅️ FinMap Unit =?= TreeMap Nat Unit compare ▼
--             [] ✅️ TreeMap Nat Unit compare =?= TreeMap Nat Unit compare
--       [isDefEq] ✅️ ?m.4 =?= instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2 ▼
--         [] ?m.4 [assignable] =?= instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2 [nonassignable]
--         [assign] ✅️ ?m.4 := instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2 ▼
--           [beforeMkLambda] ?m.4 [] := instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2
--           [checkTypes] ✅️ (?m.4 : OFE (FinMap Unit)) := (instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2 : OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit)) ▼
--             [] ✅️ OFE (FinMap Unit) =?= OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▼
--               [] ✅️ FinMap Unit =?= (fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit ▼
--                 [] ✅️ FinMap Unit =?= TreeMap Nat Unit compare ▼
--                   [] ✅️ TreeMap Nat Unit compare =?= TreeMap Nat Unit compare
--     [answer] ✅️ OFE (FinMap Unit)
--   [isDefEq] ✅️ OFE (FinMap Unit) =?= OFE ((fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit) ▼
--     [] ✅️ FinMap Unit =?= (fun x => TreeMap Nat x compare) Unit ▼
--       [] ✅️ FinMap Unit =?= TreeMap Nat Unit compare ▼
--         [] ✅️ TreeMap Nat Unit compare =?= TreeMap Nat Unit compare
--   [] result instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2
-- [Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ ?m.3 =?= instOFETreeMapNatCompareUnit_issue2 ▶
-- [Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ OFE (FinMap Unit) =?= OFE (FinMap Unit)

My understanding of it is that the inference reduces (TreeMap Nat · compare) Unit to TreeMap Nat Unit compare before trying to unify it with an application, and then understandably gets very confused while trying to solve the subsequent constraint.
What I don't understand is why it does that, and why the problem disapears when using an abbreviation.
I would be happy if someone could enlighten me on these subjects :)

I should also note that I am using lean 4.29.0.

Here is an even simpler code where the issue arises (in particular it does not need Iris or anything really)

class FOO (X : Type)
instance (M : Type -> Type) X : FOO (M X) where

instance : FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) := by infer_instance
-- the line above fails

abbrev ID : Type -> Type := fun x => x
instance : FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) := by infer_instance
-- the line above succeeds

And here are the typeclass inference traces

trace for the unsuccessfull typeclass resolution

[Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= ?m.3 ▶
[Meta.synthInstance] ❌️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ▼
  [] ✅️ new goal FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ▶
  [apply] ❌️ apply instFOO to FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ▼
    [tryResolve] ❌️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ≟ FOO (?m.6 ?m.7) ▼
      [isDefEq] ❌️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= FOO (?m.6 ?m.7) ▼
        [] ❌️ (fun x => x) Unit =?= ?m.6 ?m.7 ▼
          [] (fun x => x) Unit [nonassignable] =?= ?m.6 ?m.7 [assignable]
          [assign] ❌️ ?m.6 ?m.7 := (fun x => x) Unit ▼
            [foApprox] ?m.6 [?m.7] := (fun x => x) Unit
            [foApprox] ?m.6 [?m.7] := PUnit
            [constApprox] ?m.6 [?m.7] := (fun x => x) Unit
          [assign] ❌️ ?m.6 ?m.7 := PUnit ▼
            [foApprox] ?m.6 [?m.7] := PUnit
            [constApprox] ?m.6 [?m.7] := PUnit
        [onFailure] ❌️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= FOO (?m.6 ?m.7)
        [onFailure] ❌️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= FOO (?m.6 ?m.7)
  [] result <not-available>
[Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= FOO ((fun x => x) Unit)

trace for the successfull typeclass inference (with the abbrev)

[Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= ?m.3 ▶
[Meta.synthInstance] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ▼
  [] ✅️ new goal FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ▼
    [instances] #[instFOO, instFOOUnit]
  [apply] ✅️ apply instFOOUnit to FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ▼
    [tryResolve] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ≟ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) ▼
      [isDefEq] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= FOO ((fun x => x) Unit)
      [isDefEq] ✅️ ?m.5 =?= instFOOUnit ▼
        [] ?m.5 [assignable] =?= instFOOUnit [nonassignable]
        [assign] ✅️ ?m.5 := instFOOUnit ▼
          [beforeMkLambda] ?m.5 [] := instFOOUnit
          [checkTypes] ✅️ (?m.5 : FOO ((fun x => x) Unit)) := (instFOOUnit : FOO ((fun x => x) Unit)) ▼
            [] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= FOO ((fun x => x) Unit)
    [answer] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit)
  [isDefEq] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= FOO ((fun x => x) Unit)
  [] result instFOOUnit
[Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ ?m.4 =?= instFOOUnit ▶
[Meta.isDefEq] ✅️ FOO ((fun x => x) Unit) =?= FOO ((fun x => x) Unit)

The instance instance (M : Type -> Type) X : FOO (M X) where is hard for lean to apply, because M and X need to be determined by unifying M X with the target. This is a higher order unification which doesn't have a unique solution.
